skill.name: plan-writing
skill.description: Helps create concise implementation plans with ordered tasks, dependencies, verification checks, and done criteria for multi-step software work.
skill.summary: Create concise, verifiable plans for multi-step software work.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Multi-step coding work can become vague, large, and hard to verify. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create short plans with clear tasks, order, and checks.
actual_capabilities: Breaks complex software work into short, ordered actions.
Defines a clear goal and done criteria for each plan.
Adds verification checks to planned tasks.
Adapts plans for new projects, features, bug fixes, and refactors.
Encourages project-specific scripts instead of generic command lists.
Keeps plans concise and avoids fixed templates.
limitations: Does not execute tasks or run verification commands.
Does not inspect files beyond what the host agent reads.
Does not replace engineering judgment for architecture or security choices.
May need user context for ambiguous scope, stack, or acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Plan a feature build
use_cases.description: Create a short implementation plan with ordered tasks, affected areas, and verification checks.

use_cases.title: Organize a refactor
use_cases.description: Break a refactor into safe steps with dependencies, review points, and clear completion criteria.

use_cases.title: Clarify a bug fix
use_cases.description: Turn a complex defect into a focused fix plan with root cause checks and test expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plan-writing to create a short plan for this task: [describe task]. Include a goal, tasks, and done criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a feature change
prompt_templates.scenario: Feature work with known product requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plan-writing for this feature: [feature]. Include likely affected files, dependencies, task order, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Refactoring across several files or modules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plan-writing to plan this refactor: [scope]. Keep tasks small, identify dependencies, and define safe verification after each step.

prompt_templates.title: Plan complex delivery
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with risks, sequencing, and validation needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plan-writing to create a concise delivery plan for [project]. Include critical path, parallel work, risk checks, and final verification.

output_examples.input: Add password reset to an existing web application.
output: Goal: Add a secure password reset flow.
Tasks: confirm current auth flow; add request step; add reset step; connect email delivery; verify valid and invalid token behavior.
Done when users can reset passwords and invalid tokens fail safely.

output_examples.input: Refactor the settings area into smaller modules.
output: Goal: Split settings code without changing user behavior.
Tasks: map current settings flow; extract shared state; move each section; update imports; verify settings still save correctly.
Done when existing settings behavior passes manual and automated checks.
Goal: Identify and fix the checkout failure path.
Tasks: reproduce the failure; inspect payment and cart state; patch the root cause; add a regression check; verify successful checkout.
Done when the failure no longer reproduces under the documented scenario.

best_practices: Provide the task goal, stack, known files, and acceptance criteria before planning.
Keep every task tied to one clear verification check.
Revise the plan when discovery changes the scope or order.
anti_patterns: Requesting a long template when the task needs a short checklist.
Using generic setup steps without naming the actual project context.
Treating the plan as complete when verification criteria are missing.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and verification ideas only.

faq.question: What tasks fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits feature work, refactors, bug fixes, and new project planning.

faq.question: How detailed should the input be?
faq.answer: Provide the goal, current context, known constraints, and any required acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Can it create long project plans?
faq.answer: It is designed for concise plans. Very large work should be split into separate plans.

faq.question: Does it require a specific framework?
faq.answer: No. It adapts the plan to the project type and technology you describe.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
